goal: Teach Year-2 physics students to move from a familiar vertical-motion model to named MATLAB variables, sampled arrays, element-wise operations, a labelled plot, and one executable physical validation check.

deck_context.source_summary: This Week 01 lecture repairs uncertain MATLAB foundations through one familiar model: a ball launched vertically upward with air resistance neglected. Students predict the motion, identify variables and units, create a time array, use MATLAB indexing and element-wise operators, plot height against time, and validate the known launch value.
deck_context.core_claim: A physical model becomes trustworthy computational evidence only when its variables, arrays, operations, plot, and validation check stay connected.

predictions: falls back toward the launch height
locked_model.required_validation: y(0) = 0 m, represented in MATLAB as y_m(1)

sample_generation_method.input_context_preparation: Parent inspected the selected Theme 1 mockup, the strict vertical-motion asset, and all slide-level source assets with view_image before delegation.
sample_generation_method.handoff_rule: Subagents must use this same built-in image tool, image-edit mode, and local-image context preparation; return a blocker if unavailable.

style.name: Teaching Courseware — Muted Academic Blue + Sage

slides.title: Decide what the computer must remember
slides.intent: Make variables, parameters, outputs, arrays, meanings, and units concrete before code.
key_points: Scalars store fixed values such as y0, v0, and g.
An array stores many chosen times.
Every stored quantity needs a meaning and unit.
slides.local_context: Map y0 -> y0_m -> m, v0 -> v0_mps -> m s^-1, g -> g_mps2 -> m s^-2, t -> t_s -> s, and y(t) -> y_m -> m. Distinguish a fixed parameter from an array of sampled values.

slides.title: Sampling is a choice, not the motion itself
slides.intent: Connect arrays to selected physical moments without confusing the sampled representation with the underlying model.
key_points: t_s = 0:0.1:4 and linspace(0,4,41) make 41 time samples.
The endpoints and count match.
Sampling changes what we see, not the underlying equation.
slides.local_context: Use t_s = 0:0.1:4 and t_s = linspace(0,4,41) exactly. Both describe time in seconds from 0 to 4 s. Show the continuous idea as a smooth trajectory with selected sample moments.

slides.title: One index represents one physical moment
slides.intent: Turn one-based indexing into a physical interpretation skill.
key_points: t_s(1) is the launch time.
t_s(11) selects 1.0 s.
An index is a storage location, not a time value.
slides.local_context: Use the 41-sample array from 0:0.1:4 s. Make t_s(1) = 0.0 s and t_s(11) = 1.0 s explicit, and remind learners that MATLAB indexing starts at 1.

slides.title: Make one equation work for many times
slides.intent: Show how a physical equation becomes an array calculation while preserving units.
key_points: Start from y(t) = y0 + v0 t - (1/2) g t^2.
Each stored time gets one height.
Every term on the right has units of metres.
slides.local_context: Use upward positive and air resistance neglected. Explain the three contributions: starting position, launch contribution, and gravity contribution. Use a small array output preview, not a full code block.

slides.title: The missing dot changes the operation
slides.intent: Isolate the most important Week 1 distinction: scalar arithmetic versus element-wise array operations.
key_points: 20 * 3 produces one scalar.
v0_mps .* t_s produces one value per time.
t_s.^2 squares every stored time value.
slides.local_context: Use the exact MATLAB fragments 20 * 3, v0_mps .* t_s, and t_s.^2. Explain that the dot means apply the operation element by element. Keep the discussed dot as the only strongly emphasised operator.

slides.title: Use a check the model must pass
slides.intent: Show the minimum executable physical check before trusting a result.
key_points: The known condition is y(0) = 0 m.
In a one-based array this is y_m(1).
A smooth graph is not enough.
slides.local_context: Connect the known launch condition to the first stored value. Render the exact executable check assert(abs(y_m(1)-y0_m) < 1e-12) and show a passing state. The supplied equation assets provide y(1) = 0.000 m and t = 0 s.

slides.title: State what the computation lets us claim
slides.intent: Move from reading code to making a defensible physics statement.

The array and plot show sampled positions.
The check supports the starting boundary condition.
A result needs a unit, a trend, and a limitation.
slides.local_context: Use the vertical-motion example to distinguish supported claims from overclaims. The evidence chain is model, sampling, operation, plot, and validation. Include one small wrong-claim versus supported-claim contrast.
